actions.item: Recruit additional workers (ideal 1 worker per 14 ha, 1 harvester per 22 ha)
Resume Rhinoceros beetle treatment in P24F and immature replants
Study the flooding pattern in the ~800 ha low-lying area and propose a solution
Raise machine productivity: 1 machine per 140 ha, 5 harvesters per machine (target 12–15 t/day)
Expedite delayed 2026 manuring (7 of 415.25 t by Feb); avoid manuring in Nov–Dec monsoon
Start drainage works after floods: desilt drains and clear blocked culverts
Road grading, lateriting and patching in flood-hit low-lying roads; inspect roads in rain for scupper drains/sumps
Palm census across all areas with PARAS GIS team support (palm counting and mapping)
Ganoderma census and treatment in tall-palm fields; de-bole and shred stumps, expose roots to sun
Install more barn owl nests to reach 139 (1 per 15 ha)
Add Cassia cobanensis to beneficial plants
Grass-cut harvester paths with a roto-slasher to avoid overspraying
Restack fronds in flood-affected low-lying areas
Evacuate harvested FFB along smallholder / Kampung Asli boundary the same day
Consider lower-risk areas for future supplying in P21A, P22C, P22D
P24F: prevent cover crop creeping onto palms; ablation now palms are 14 months; review banana interplanting
P25G: complete infilling of vacant points (148 design); spot-spray Rhinoceros with Cypermethrin/Carbofuran
Apply EFB in lateritic soil areas (not started; 2025 budget 2,900 mt)
P22E1/E2 abandoned and categorised unplantable
Reduce overripe bunches: closer harvest supervision, keep 15-day interval
Knock out loose fruit from excessively overripe bunches (rotten heap in P96Y2)
Remove dry hanging fronds; raise progressive pruning to satisfactory standard
Fix hanging-type roadside drains whose outlets sit above the road surface
Kieserite 1,000 g per palm to Mg-deficient palms in P21A3; monitor other sub-blocks
Eradicate weeds at vacant points during selective spraying; check sprayed areas after two weeks and touch up
Weeding plan: 3 selective, 2 circle, 1 spot round; one-sided nozzle or baffle in soft-grass areas
Quarterly rat census in young mature areas; group sub-blocks above 10% and bait in one direction
Yearly barn owl census; clean boxes without eggs or chicks
Annual palm census after floods in P21A, P21B, P22D, P22C, P24F, P25G; supply quickly to 148 SPH; raise planting points by 1 ft
Ganoderma census to include de-boled and toppled palms
Investigate wet floor in fertiliser store (leaks, rain through vents)
Rhinoceros beetle: keep Alika ZC, spray early morning/evening at entry points with spreader-sticker
P21A2: remove mud from shoots, repeat spray after 7–10 days if wet, watch for shoot rot
P24F weed-mulch: monitor soil moisture, consider non-woven hydrophilic mulch; remove LLDPE after 2 years
Watermelon contractors: no ploughing within 1 ft of seedling canopy edge (P26H)
Plant Mucuna where contractors are not working; soft grasses on cambered bunds
Root-prune overgrown seedlings and harden 2 weeks before field planting
Compact soil at planting to stop slant-planted palms (P26H)
Monitor burn marks on chipped trunk stacks in dry spells (fire risk)
Ganoderma SOP in replants: 1.5 m de-bole holes open 2–3 months, 29 x 29 ft (148 SPH), silt survey, 2-ft drains in cambered bunds
Drainage feasibility study using DEM/topographic map for replanting areas; structured annual desilting
After delays, manure young mature and prime palms before over-mature palms
Minimise gap between fertiliser schedule and actual application

kb:
LADANG SUNGAI MARUNG - FACT PACK (Far East Holdings Berhad, Far East group). Regional Senior Manager En. Musa bin Abdul Halim; Estate Manager En. Mohd Awis Bin Md Akin; Assistant Manager Muhamad Ridzuan bin Md Ramli (from Nov 2025).

SOURCES. (1) PA Report 1/2026 (Planting Advisory), visit 16 March 2026 (introduction says 18 March), period reviewed January to December 2025 and January to February 2026, Planting Advisor En. Mohd Sufian Bin Yusoff. Previous PA visit 10 September 2025 (PA 2/2025, Jan-Aug 2025). (2) Agronomy Report 1/2026, visit 3 March 2026, Senior Agronomist Mr. Lai Hong Heng; previous visit 12 November 2025 (Agronomy 2/2025, which set the 2026 programme, later amended).

AREA (PA 1/2026). Total 2,264.90 ha. 2026: mature 1,145.50 ha (934.11 + Sg Gayung Division 123.10 + Sg Marung Division 88.29), immature 712.73 ha, replanting 282.00 ha (P26H), total planted 2,140.23 ha, buildings 4.17 ha, unplantable 120.50 ha (up from 10.50 after P22E and 30 ha of P22C were abandoned after floods). 2025: mature 1,423.50, immature 455.73, replanting 371.00. Age profile (Agro): 47% over 26 years (1,014.7 ha), 33% 0-3 years, 19% 4-7, none 8-19, 1% 20-25. Main fields (ha): P94K 375.60, P94M 328.79, P95S 155.91, P95T 69.10 (74.40 before 5.30 ha went to P26H), P96Y 85.30 (Y1, Y2; was 362), P05W 18.80, P21A 138, P21B 108, P22D 105, P22C 50, P24F 212.73, P25G 206, P26H 282. SPH (census): P94K 127, P94M 125, P95S 128, P95T 125, P96Y 128, P05W 120, young plantings 142-148; estate 136.

CROP (PA 1/2026 section 8, 1,185.51 ha mature). Jan-Dec 2025 FFB 19,296.70 t vs budget 19,100.00 t (+2%); 2024 20,547.89 t. Yield 16.28 t/ha vs budget 16.11; 2024 18.16. CPO 3,662.45 t, OER 18.98%, KER 4.77%. Highest fields 2025: P05W 27.11 t/ha, P94M 20.50; lowest P95S 15.95, P96Y 15.09 (flood-prone). Jan-Feb 2026 FFB 3,209.70 t, 23% above budget and in line with the same period of 2025. PA 2/2025: Jan-Aug 2025 13,171.37 t (11.11 t/ha) vs budget 11,380 t and 11,820.40 t same period 2024. Scout harvesting: P21A 15 ha gave 245 t in 2025; P22D 318.70 t in 12 months. P21B declared mature 2025: 838.92 t = 9.12 t/ha Jan-Aug 2025.

YIELD HISTORY (Agro 1/2026 chart, t/ha): 2019 18.08, 2020 21.38, 2021 19.17, 2022 14.20, 2023 15.03, 2024 19.50, 2025 16.88. Agro Table 19 2025 vs 2024: P94K 17 vs 19.79, P94M 20.41 vs 22.26, P95S 15.95 vs 19.95, P95T 16.42 vs 17, P96Y 15.09 vs 16.66, P05W 27.11 vs 28.51; average drop 2.62 t/ha (13.65%), blamed on floods in Mar and mid-Apr 2025 that cut off P94K, P95S and P96Y for about 40 days. Agro 2/2025: bunch weight steady, bunches per palm fell from 5.9 (2024) to 5.4 (Jan-Oct 2025). Older tonnes (Agro 2/2024 Appendix 3): 2020 28,619.87 t, 2021 23,815.45, 2022 18,122.80, 2023 16,856.84. Note the PA and Agro estate yields differ (see issues).

COST (PA 1/2026, Jan-Dec 2025). Ex-estate cost RM280.79/t FFB vs budget RM356.02 (-21%): general charges RM95.14 (budget 140.99), upkeep and cultivation RM80.37 (102.01), harvesting and collection RM105.28 (113.01): harvesting 59.73, internal transport 30.11, external transport 15.44. Processing RM70.00, palm oil transport 7.41, cess 37.67, depreciation 25.70; total RM421.57/t vs 461.94. General charges RM1,835,882.30 = RM1,190.42/ha on 1,542.21 ha vs RM1,746.18 (-32%); overspent items staff welfare (Family Day), paid leave/VLP RM127,556.51 (+32%), SOCSO, medical VMO, recruitment RM199,438.28 vs RM74,560 (66 foreign workers vs 30 budgeted), all-risk insurance, workmen compensation (deceased worker), MSPO/ISCC RM14,751.91. Upkeep RM1,550,830 = RM1,308.15/ha on 1,185.51 ha vs RM1,643.56: weeding 223.20 (249.12), manuring 633.69 (821.48), pest and disease 90.52 (111.85), census 6.86 (19.52), drains 71.96 (81.47), roads 98.51 (153.32), pruning 176.69 (188.80).

LABOUR AND STAFF (PA 1/2026, Feb 2026). 143 workers vs requirement 140 (1 worker per 15 ha): harvesters 75 (req 73), drivers/loaders 6 (15), weeding 21 (16), manuring 14 (12), general 3 (8), others 24 (16). 41 checkroll, 102 contract. Up from 113 at the last visit; 54 recruited in 2025, 20 repatriated, 16 absconded. Harvester ratio 1:18 ha over 1,145.50 ha mature plus 243 ha scout harvesting. Concluding remarks quote 151 workers.

HARVESTING (PA and Agro). Average interval 15 days, 23.58 rounds in 2025; extended in P95S, P95T, P96Y. Jan-Feb 2026 intervals up to 23 days in P95S and P96Y. 70% of FFB direct to Sawira POM, 30% via ramp to Merchong POM. Mechanisation 2025: MBI 9 units 8.22 t/day, Timac 4 units 10.22 t/day, Badang 1 unit 8.25 t/day; 46 harvesters, 1 machine to 3.5 harvesters; harvesters about 3 t/day. PA recommends 1 machine per 140 ha and 5 harvesters per machine. Agro: overripe bunches are the main yield loss with no improvement: P94K5 5%, P94K8 8%, P94K9 10%, P94M4 8% (Mar 2026); rotten bunch heap in P96Y2.

MANURING. 2025 completed (PA: required 915.55 t, applied 927.95 t, balance 104.27 t; Agro: 851.25 t, 100% by Nov 2025; Mix B delayed in flooded young blocks). 2026 to Feb: 7.00 t applied of 415.25 t required (Jan NK2 in progress; Feb NK2 183.85 t, Mix B 47.35, Compound 25 29.00, Compound 44 22.80 not started) due to heavy rain Nov 2025-Feb 2026 and floods. Semi-mechanised application 35-40 bags per worker per day; RM2.00-2.50 per bag, about RM75/day.

2026 FERTILISER PROGRAMME (Agro 1/2026 Appendix 1, revised, grams per palm). P94K: NK2 2,500 Feb. P94M: NK2 2,500 Jan. P95S and P95T: NK2 2,000 Feb and Sep. P96Y1-Y2: NK2 2,000 Jan and Sep (Y3-Y8 replanted). P05W: NK2 2,000 Feb, NK2 1,500 Jun, Mix B 1,500 Oct. P21A and P21B: Mix B 1,750 Feb, 1,500 May, RP 2,000 Jun, Mix B 1,500 Aug and Nov; supply palms Comp B 1,000 Feb, 1,200 May, RP 2,000 Jun, Comp B 1,200 Aug and Nov. P22D: Mix B 1,500 Feb, May, Aug, Nov, RP 2,000 Jun. P24F: Comp A 1,000 Feb, May, Aug, RP 1,750 Oct, Comp A 1,200 Nov. P22C (printed P25/C 80 ha): Comp A 800 May, RP 1,500 Jun, Comp A 900 Aug, 1,000 Nov. P25G: Comp A 800 Mar, RP 1,500 Apr, Comp A 900 Jun, 1,000 Sep and Dec. P26: 600 g CRF + 500 g RP at planting, Comp A 800 month 10, RP 1,500 month 11. No manuring for blocks replanting in 2026-2027. The Nov 2025 draft had a second NK2 round for P94K (Aug) and P94M (Jul), Mix B in P95S/P95T/P96Y/P05W and 1,750 g Mix B rounds for P21A/B. 2025 programme (Agro 2/2024): NK2 2,500 x2 in P94K and M1-M3, <NK2 2,000> x2 in M4, M5, M11, Mix A 2,000 x3 in P95S, P95T, P96Y, Mix A 2,000 x4 + RP 1,500 in P05W.

WEEDING. 2025 circle and path 98% (P94M11 2 of 3 rounds, flooding); selective 100%. Feb 2026: circle 456.80 ha (77%), selective 980.54 ha (87%). Agro: ground vegetation borderline acceptable (52% sparse, 36% acceptable soft grass, 12% grassy low-lying), sporadic Clidemia, Stenochlaena, Dicranopteris, VOPs. Recommended 3 selective, 2 circle, 1 spot round.

PRUNING. 2025 progressive pruning 1,414.82 of 1,423.50 ha (99%). Agro: quality improved, slightly above acceptable, sporadic dry hanging fronds; slight over-pruning in P21A3.

PESTS AND DISEASES. Rats below 10% in tall palms (Jan 2026: P94K 8.30, P94M 6.80, P95S 8.70, P96Y 5.30%); P21B 13.40% and P21A 12.60% in Jan 2026 fell to 9.40% and 8.90% after baiting. 73 barn owl nests (PA 100% occupied, Agro 90%), target 139. No bagworm in 2025. Rhinoceros beetle controlled with Alika ZC every 3 weeks in P21A supply, P24F, P25G. Ganoderma: P96Y census Jun 2025 8.59%; P94K and P94M in progress; P95S, P95T, P05W not started. Mg deficiency in flood-prone P21A3: kieserite 1 kg per palm. Foliar (Mar 2025 samples): P05W N 2.59, K 1.00, Mg 0.29; P21A N 2.61, K 1.12, Mg 0.28; P21B1 Mg 0.24.

FLOODS AND DRAINS. Three floods mid-Dec 2025 to mid-Jan 2026 affected 363 ha mature and 446 ha immature; about 800 ha low-lying, five inlets from neighbours and Kampung Asli, outlet Sungai Rompin. Agro lists 318 ha flood-prone in mature sub-blocks (P95S3 100%, P95S4 85%, P96Y4 67%, P96Y3 63%). Desilting 2025 470.54 chains (programme 1,400-1,460). Road grading 2,291 of 4,810 chains in 2025.

IMMATURE AND REPLANTING. P21A: 4,776 palms planted on 30 flooded ha; cost to maturity RM3,085.49/ha (budget 3,474.33). P22D: 1,650 supplied; RM2,987.00 (3,356.40). P22C: 50 ha replanted May 2025, 2,713 palms; other 30 ha abandoned. P24F (212.73 ha): good Mucuna on terraces, palms 14 months, ready for ablation, banana and watermelon intercrops. P25G (206 ha): 29,086 palms, infilling in progress, watermelon lease 2 years, cost RM8,415.63/ha (10,449.25). P26H (282 ha ex-P96Y3-8 and part of P95T5): felling Jan-Feb 2026, bunds 60%, planting 25% (Agro) to about 50% (PA). Replanting plan 2027 277.30 ha, 2028 309.19, 2029 273.81, 2030 173.20.

RAINFALL (mm, days). 2021 2,550/120, 2022 2,416/124, 2023 4,643/167, 2024 4,756/138, 2025 3,309/148 (Dec 2025 1,034.5 mm). Five-year average 3,535 mm.

KEY ACTIONS. Recruit workers; resume Rhinoceros treatment; study flooding; improve machine ratio; expedite 2026 manuring; desilt drains; Ganoderma census; more owl boxes; cut overripe bunches; fix pruning quality; quarterly rat census in young mature; palm census after floods; apply EFB.
